title: Safe auxiliary model assistance and tier routing
summary: Add inherited routing configuration, bounded availability fallback and opt-in advisory validation triage.

request_parts.text: Research and refine the request with primary sources and measurable acceptance.
Resolve global and per-plan tier primary/fallback configuration with strict validation.
Fallback on availability at the same logical rung without semantic failure evidence.
Persist bounded cooldown and resumable pause when all allowed providers are unavailable.
Provide one multiple-choice configuration question per setting with authenticated provider discovery.
Reject unsupported per-model effort combinations before provider dispatch.
Add opt-in budgeted advisory validation triage with bounded redacted evidence.
Enforce a fail-closed no-write assistant boundary and keep failure classification authoritative.
Commit each validated task with a retained resumable plan and regression evidence.
Review the complete skill and preserve direct mode, prompt budgets and existing workflows.

repository_findings: Quota events leave functional_failures unchanged and the runner retries the same provider.
Existing CI fails the entrypoint character budget before tests run.
Code inspection confirms quota events do not alter the provider candidate set.
Provider selection uses functional failures while availability failures only retry or abort.
Plan creation writes a full defaults snapshot and quota failures preserve semantic counters.
The unmodified entrypoint exceeds its existing fixed character budget.
request_analysis.research_decision: Broad primary-source study requested; retain bounded decision evidence in docs/research/AUXILIARY_ROUTING.md.
research_findings: Parallel research benefits from bounded specialists, but the reported multi-agent system used roughly 15 times chat tokens. This is workload-specific, not a universal saving.
Simple routing and orchestrator-worker workflows are preferable to unnecessary autonomous coordination. Evaluation needs explicit success criteria.
Context is a finite resource; task-scoped retrieval and compact handoffs reduce irrelevant context.
Code-driven orchestration offers explicit control; manager-tool and handoff patterns have different ownership semantics.
Controlled configurations show coordination benefits depend on task structure; sequential tasks can suffer overhead and error amplification.
Architecture experiments favor selective feedback and summary-based communication; effectiveness depends on task and model capability.
Budget-conditioned coordination can suppress redundant interactions in its experimental setting.
tools empty disables built-ins but not MCP; restricted mode and settings controls matter. auth status exits zero when logged in.
codex login status checks credential presence without a generation request. Read-only is distinct from workspace-write.
The sandbox permits writes in its workspace. Sandbox enabled alone is not a read-only guarantee.
Permission controls and sandboxing are distinct from a tool-less advisory role. CLI versions and affordances differ.
assumptions: Use host-managed execution; no independent provider CLI is available here.
risks: Provider CLI capabilities differ across versions; native behavior needs separate verification.
Native provider/OS support varies and cannot be inferred from mocked success.
request_analysis.decomposition_strategy: Split configuration, availability, wizard and triage by their independent contracts and tests; finish with whole-skill review.
